newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Dec 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Dec 18.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The vice-chairman of parliament and the leader of the Civic Democratic Alliance, Jan Kalvoda, resigned from government and from his party. He announced that he is not, as he had claimed, a doctor of law and that using this title was a big mistake.
- The most likely way of solving the crisis at Poldi steel is to call a tender, the National Property Fund said. Vladimir Stehlik resigned from his post as general manager yesterday from prison.

- The largest domestic black coal mining company, OKD, is meeting with powerful competition from Polish mining companies. OKD intends to request that the Ministry of Industry and Trade implement stronger import restrictions on coal.

- The Czech National Bank approved the transformation of Brno's branch of Austria's Osterreichische Volksbanken AG to Volksbank a.s.. Volksbank a.s. will begin operations on January 1, 1997 and will take over all the loans and deposits from the Austrian branch.

- The Czech National Bank posted a further decrease in the growth rate of M2 money in October. The year-to-year increase in October was 11.4 percent, not including SPT Telecom deposits, while the M2 growth rate was 13.8 percent in September.
- Large domestic demand, the approaching Christmas holidays and a lack of alternative investment opportunities has resulted in a "buying fever" on the domestic retail market.

- Chemopetrol received a seven-year syndicated loan worth 230 million marks (four billion crowns) from 14 domestic and foreign banks. The transaction was arranged by London's Citibank International Plc.
- Moravia Steel obtained an eight-year loan worth two billion crowns. The loan was arranged by Ceska Sporitelna.
- The Tatra automobile company, expecting losses of 770 million crowns in 1996, expects to post a gross profit of 70 million crowns in 1997, according to a spokesman for the company, Ivo Celechovsky.

- The Czech government approved the text of the Czech-German declaration without making any changes. The German government is facing further requests for changes to the declaration from the Bavarian government.

- The largest domestic manufacturer of tires, Barum Continental s.r.o., will produce 5.4 million tires this year, an increase of nearly one million from the year before. The company expects to increase production to 10 million by 1999.
PRAVO - The Czech Senate will sit for the first time in history today in the knight's hall of the Valdstejn Palace.
- The Ministry of Finance has instituted forced administration on the AgB IF 2 investment fund, according to Marie Jezkova from the ministry.
- Tesla Telekomunikace s.r.o. won an international tender for supplying Lithuania with digital equipment for the country's telecommunications system. The tender is worth $2.5 million.
- Investicni a Postovni Banka has decided against selling its 38 percent share in Svit a.s..
- Ceskoslovenska Obchodni Banka obtained a majority share in Finop, according to the spokesman for the bank, Milan Tomanek.
- Motokov Praha will likely purchase Zetor a.s., the Brno-based tractor manufacturer since Motokov is the only company still interested in purchasing the company, according to unnamed sources.
